## Intro:

- In R functions are quite straightforward. Imagine we have a data frame with variable that we wish to perform some arrgregates on, and for simplicity let's use the `gss` data from `forcats`:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
gss <- forcats::gss_cat
# readr::write_csv(gss, "Data/R4DS/gss.csv")
```

- Imagine now we want to perform some operations on this data in order to generate an output file. For that, we need a `data frame function`, i.e., a function that takes a data frame as input and produces a data frame as output:

```{r}
prop_data <- function(df, var) {
  # Set label using rlang:
  lbs <- rlang::as_label(enquo(var)) |>
    str_to_title() |>
    str_replace_all("_", " ")

  # Data frame function
  data <- df |>
    mutate({{ var }} := forcats::as_factor({{ var }})) |>
    count({{ var }}, .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
      prop = n / sum(n),
      prop_pct = (n / sum(n)) |> scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1),
      is_na = if_else({{ var }} %in% c("No answer"), "Yes", "No"),
      n_valid = if_else(is_na == "Yes", NA_real_, n),
      prop_valid = if_else(
        is_na == "Yes",
        NA_real_,
        n_valid / sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      prop_valid_pct = if_else(
        is_na == "Yes",
        NA_real_,
        (n_valid / sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE))
      ) |>
        scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1),
      n_tot = sum(n),
      n_tot_valid = sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_na = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n, NA_real_),
      na_prop = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n_na / sum(n), NA_real_),
      na_prop_pct = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n_na / sum(n), NA_real_) |>
        scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1),
      color_palet = "steelblue"
    )

  max_n <- max(data$n_valid, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_p <- max(data$prop_valid, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Use cli to showcase:
  cli::cli_h1("data: {lbs}")
  print(data)

  # Plot:
  cli::cli_h1("Plot: {lbs}")
  p <- data |>
    ggplot(aes(x = prop_valid, y = {{ var }}, fill = color_palet)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = scales::percent(prop_valid, accuracy = 1)),
      size = 4,
      vjust = 0.5,
      hjust = -0.1
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(),
      labels = scales::label_percent(),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)),
      limits = c(0, NA)
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.1))
    ) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    labs(y = lbs, x = "", ) +
    theme_classic(base_family = "aptos", base_size = 11)
  print(p)

  # return data quietly:
  invisible(list(
    data = data, 
    label = lbs, 
    plot = p, 
    max_n = max_n)
    )
}
t <- gss |> prop_data(marital)
```

- This setup above could be thought of as a 'God-function',
